The Fricke primary standard is used to determine the absorbed dose to water.
The Fricke solution is calibrated using a two-step procedure.
The energy range considered in this paper is 6-20 MeV.
The correction factor proposed for all MeV qualities is k = 1.012 ± 0.010.
The method used to determine the absorbed dose to water is a chemical Fricke (ferrous ammonium sulfate) dosimeter.
The Monte Carlo simulation is used to calculate energy losses due to absorption in materials upstream of the vessel, backscattering, and Bremsstrahlung.
High-energy electrons are used in this paper.
The response of the alanine dosemeter for high-energy electrons is independent of energy.
The magnetic spectrometer is used to determine the energy spectrum of the incident electrons.
The Faraday cup is used to detect the incident electrons.
The total absorption experiment uses a monoenergetic electron beam.
The polymethylmethacrylate phantom is used in this paper.
The Fricke solution is filled in LDPE bags for irradiation.
The bags are carefully filled with fresh Fricke solution using a glass pipette.
The bags are heat-sealed leaving a 0.5 cm gas gap between the Fricke solution and the seal.
The bags are inserted into a polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) holder.
The holder guarantees that the 3 cm × 4 cm × 0.3 cm volume occupied by the Fricke solution is identical for all bags.
The bags are left in the phantom at least 10 min before irradiation starts to ensure temperature equilibrium of the Fricke solution with the surrounding water.
The water temperature, air pressure, and relative humidity are measured continuously.
